stepNotes.1: Single Hono route module, 122 LOC, one lazy export IsolationRoutes (isolation.ts:33) with GET isolation.get and PUT isolation.set; owns only IsolationMode/IsolationState Zod schemas.
stepNotes.2: Asset surface is the process-global AX_CODE_ISOLATION_MODE/NETWORK env vars; isolation flags are absent from ScopedFlagName (scoped.ts:21,31), so writes are last-writer-wins across directories — the dominant cross-project contamination threat.
stepNotes.3: GET re-derives from config every call and force-syncs env; PUT uses the requested mode/network for the response because env holds the stale value until persistProjectConfigFeatureResponse updates it (isolation.ts:94-100), both verified by passing tests.
stepNotes.4: No sync CPU work or loops; persist is serialized by Lock.write + FileLock.acquire (project-config.ts:140-141). System-level concern is that every GET mutates a process-global env var, invalidating other directories' policy.
stepNotes.5: Dual state derivation (route-local isolationConfigState vs Isolation.resolve) reconciled by one-way env overwrite on GET; cleanest long-term fix is the scoped-flag pattern already used for autonomous/super-long, but that change is larger than this unit.
stepNotes.6: No dead exports, empty catches, or TODOs; the only contract gap is the undeclared 500 response on PUT persist failure (isolation.ts:74-84 vs line 116), leaving the generated SDK without an error schema.
stepNotes.7: test/server/isolation.test.ts has 9 focused tests covering config-over-env authority, backend/protected preservation, stale-env PUT response, and string network parsing; gaps are the 500 path, the read-only+network:true coercion, and any multi-directory scenario.
stepNotes.8: Five findings registered (F1 MEDIUM cross-project env contamination; F2 LOW missing 500 schema; F3 LOW GET side-effect; F4 LOW silent network coercion; F5 INFO redundant valid() call); no Critical or High.
stepNotes.9: Read source plus four local deps, runtime authority, scoped-flag layer, and the dedicated test; inline comments map 1:1 to passing tests, so documented behavior is enforced. Cleared at MEDIUM-or-below; no blocking issues for sign-off.
